question: Should OpenAI device-code authentication adopt this fixed 30-second per-operation deadline and poll-timeout retry policy after the branch is refreshed onto current main?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but the timeout changes externally observable auth-provider failure and retry semantics for slow networks and proxies, which requires owner acceptance rather than automated repair judgment.

options.title: Refresh and accept 30 seconds
options.body: Rebase onto current main, rerun focused proof, and land the shared 30-second fetch-plus-body deadline while preserving caller cancellation and the 15-minute overall poll budget.

options.title: Adjust the timeout policy
options.body: Ask the contributor to revise the duration or retry policy if auth owners consider 30 seconds too aggressive for supported proxy and network environments.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the existing unbounded request behavior until the auth owner selects a different provider-wide timeout strategy.

recommendation.title: Refresh and accept 30 seconds
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, rerun focused proof, and land the shared 30-second fetch-plus-body deadline while preserving caller cancellation and the 15-minute overall poll budget.
